Bek Lover joins Danny Jones for a talk on God, aliens, and what he calls the demonic realm. Lover is a repeat guest who reads UFO lore through a strong Christian lens. His view ties craft in the sky to spirits in scripture.

Lover argues that so-called aliens are in truth fallen beings from the Bible. He links sightings, abduction tales, and end-times signs into one frame. Jones lets him preach the frame at length, then tests it. Listeners get a faith-first take on the UFO wave. The library files the talk as an archive record of the guest's beliefs.
podcast-joerogan-71XphFGuORY:
Religion professor Diana Walsh Pasulka joins the Joe Rogan Experience for episode 2091. Pasulka wrote American Cosmic, a study of UFO belief drawn from fieldwork with scientists and experiencers. She approaches saucers the way scholars approach faith, which sets her apart from most guests on the topic.

She explains why smart people treat UFO events as sacred, and how tech leaders quietly fund the research. Rogan asks where her study left her own beliefs. The episode offers a rare angle on the phenomenon: not whether the craft are real, but why the stories around them carry such religious weight.

Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton joins Tucker Carlson to talk border strain. Carlson calls immigration the state's most pressing problem. It has changed Texas in every way, he says.

Paxton expects new federal orders to bite fast, based on past terms. He recalls politics from the Bush years onward. The title charges that George Soros shields cartels from the law. It also notes Paxton's blacklist by Fox News. Paxton presents himself as a fighter punished for his stands. The episode gives Texas voters his case in full. The fight, he insists, is far from over.
